Los grandes matemáticos también se equiv: Great mathematicians get things wrong too, and from their mistakes we learn. Pierre de Fermat was convinced that every number of the form $2^{2^n} + 1$ was prime; the first five are, and in 1732 Leonhard Euler found that the next one, $4\,294\,967\,297$, is $641 \cdot 6\,700\,417$. In 1879 Alfred Kempe published a proof of the four-colour theorem that everybody took as good for eleven years, until Percy Heawood found the step that failed. The theorem was not really proved until 1976, and with a computer's help.
Los oficios en los que un error cuesta c: Trades where a mistake costs dear do not trust memory, but checklists. Aviation adopted them in 1935, after a prototype bomber crashed on its demonstration flight because its very experienced pilots forgot to remove a control lock. Operating theatres have used them for years to confirm patient, procedure and equipment before starting. Having your own list of “mistakes I tend to make” and going over it at the end of every exam is exactly the same idea.
